LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 12.1.1 LISTENING: VIEWS/ OPINIONS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.1: Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to express one’s opinion?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. list ways of expressing views/opinions in different contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use different expressions that indicate own views/opinions in a given text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the value of one’s views/opinions as a lifelong skill in communication.  Search online and offline for the different ways of expressing views/opinions,  Listen to an oral narrative and identify the different ways used to express opinions/views,  Role-play the different characters in the narrative and bring out different ways of expressing opinions/views. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they role-play.  Explain their feelings towards issues raised in the trickster narrative. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views. Why is it important to express one’s opinion? 115  Write on a chart the words they have used to describe their feelings. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use an appropriate functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices to write.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

Why is it important to express one’s opinion? 115  Write on a chart the words they have used to describe their feelings. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use an appropriate functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices to write.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Learning to learn is enhanced as learner searches online and offline for the different ways of expressing views and opinions.

 Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner interacts using technology when searching online and listening to an oral

narrative from digital gadgets.

Values:
 Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates diverse opinions as they conduct the role play.

 Unity is achieved as the learner displays team spirit as they role play different ways of expressing opinion and views.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is enriched as learner expresses their views/opinions on different subjects.

Link to other subjects:

The concept of expressing opinions and views is a lifelong skill which is applicable in subjects such as Creative Arts and Social

Studies.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. list ways of expressing views/opinions in different contexts,
2. use different expressions that indicate own views/opinions in a given text,
3. acknowledge the value of one’s views/opinions as a lifelong skill in communication.  Search online and offline for the different ways of expressing views/opinions,  Listen to an oral narrative and identify the different ways used to express opinions/views,  Role-play the different characters in the narrative and bring out different ways of expressing opinions/views. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they role-play.  Explain their feelings towards issues raised in the trickster narrative. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views. Why is it important to express one’s opinion? 115  Write on a chart the words they have used to describe their feelings. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use an appropriate functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices to write.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to express one’s opinion?
